newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Van der Horst rebounds, rumours dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Van der Horst rebounds, rumours dismissed.

text.p: Shares in Singapore's Van der Horst rebounded early on Friday after an official denied rumours he had severed ties with the company, dealers said.
The stock on Thursday fell to its lowest level since late 1993 on various rumours, including poor results for its first half ended March 31, 1997 and delays in contracts.
At 0140 GMT, Van der Horst headed the actives rising Singapore S$0.12 to S$2.70 on volume of 3.5 million shares.
Its executive chairman Johannes Kotjo dismissed on Thursday rumours he had cut ties with the engineering-based company.

"I wished to affirm that I remain totally committed to Van der Horst as its executive chairman and I will continue to build up the group's business and help it achieve its goal of becoming a regional player in infrastructure development," he said in a statement.
Kotjo also dismissed a local newspaper report that he had lost interest in doing business in Singapore.
"Van der Horst is rebounding because Kotjo denied the rumours he was leaving, and also because the sell-off was overdone," a dealer with a foreign brokerage said.
He said he expected the shares to recover to S$2.80.
Analysts and dealers expect the company's first half results to be released either on Friday or next week.
